annotations.title: Home upgrade costs (heat pumps, solar, insulation, windows)

description: Use this when a user asks what a home upgrade costs in England and Wales (heat pumps) (country GB), Great Britain (country GB) or Ireland (country IE): a heat pump, solar panels (solar PV), loft/attic or wall insulation, or new windows. Returns an official statistic: the cost that installers or owners declared when a grant or tax claim was made (a median or average the publisher states for a period), with the period, the publisher's own wording of what the figure includes, the official source and licence. These are declared installed costs at grant or claim, not receipts, not quotes and not what one home paid; price_type is official_statistic, so the range fields can be null and the sample size is given only where the publisher states it. Each source covers only some measures: where a measure is not published the answer says so (status no_matches) instead of guessing. How fresh: England and Wales (heat pumps): monthly (the cost tables are updated each quarter, in January, April, July and October; the latest quarter ends about three months earlier); Great Britain: yearly (published each May for the financial year just ended; April to March); Ireland: irregular; the local-authority table currently ends with 2018/19. Some countries publish only a general renovation figure that is not split by type of work (the country notes say so). Do not use for a quote on a particular home, for installer prices or offers, for running costs or savings, or for other countries.

area.description: Place, only where the publisher splits by place (the country notes say how). Leave out for the national figure. GB: national figures only; an area is ignored and the answer says so. IE: a county (Kerry, Cork, Dublin, Galway...) or a local authority (Fingal, DLR, Cork City...); leave out for all of Ireland.

country.description: GB = England and Wales for heat pumps (Boiler Upgrade Scheme statistics) and Great Britain for solar panels; GB = Great Britain (solar PV: DESNZ declared installed cost per kW from MCS certificates; heat pumps: Boiler Upgrade Scheme statistics; England and Wales for heat pumps, Great Britain for solar); IE = Ireland (Revenue Home Renovation Incentive: declared value of renovation works by county; not split by type of work; SEAI figures are not included yet)

dwelling_type.description: Type of dwelling or job, only where the publisher splits by it (the country notes say which values). Leave out for the publisher's main figure. GB solar_pv: leave out for all small installations (median); or domestic, non-domestic, retrofit (domestic, existing home) or new build (domestic): these are means. GB heat_pump: not published, ignored. IE: not published, ignored.

measure.description: The upgrade: heat_pump, solar_pv, attic_insulation, wall_insulation, windows, or renovation (any home renovation works, where the publisher does not split by type). Plain words such as 'heat pump' or 'loft insulation' are accepted. GB: solar_pv (DESNZ, per kW installed) and heat_pump (Boiler Upgrade Scheme, per installation). Insulation and windows have no open GB cost statistic yet and return no_matches. IE: only renovation (any qualifying work). The Home Renovation Incentive is not split by heat pump, solar, insulation or windows, so those measures return no_matches.

size_kw.description: GB solar_pv: system size in kW; picks the DESNZ size band (0-4, 4-10 or 10-50 kW). Default: the 0-4 kW band.

technology.description: GB heat_pump: air_to_water (default), ground_source or biomass_boiler.

name: pricepaid_home_upgrade_prices

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Official published index', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Posted or listed price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.
